# Frozen before drafting: public-table transfer diagnostic

Date: 2026-10-14. User authorizes continued real validation and blind testing.
Candidate facts require an independent source check before freezing tasks.json.
Library candidate: 6825f0b1320dcf38f4ce351dd34c4b514628cef0.
Do not change runtime, retrieval or rubric based on these outputs.

Four task pairs from three published papers: VLA tradeoff analysis, VLA caption,
continual-RL analysis and visual-planning horizon analysis. Papers are absent
from the 337 source records at this candidate; model pretraining overlap unknown.
Tables are deliberately selected, not random or representative conference samples.
No original author analysis paragraph, preferred answer or invented data goes to
writers or raters. Numerical subsets and independently synthesized facts only.

Dependency: main extraction → one fresh independent fact verifier → freeze same
tasks.json bytes → two fresh writers (no-library; opt-in drafting view) → freeze
outputs → randomize each pair → two fresh anonymous LLM raters → reveal key.
Maximum three workers plus main; no worker edits another worker's file. Main
does extraction, packet construction, objective audit and result arithmetic.
Writers each see only their condition, common task file and own output path.
Raters see facts, rubric and anonymous pairs only. Keys remain private until
both ratings are frozen. Filesystem isolation is instruction-only, not sandboxed.
Fresh workers inherit model settings; immutable revision, sampling and effort
are unexposed. No repeated generation, cherry-picking or manual prose repair.
Blinding uses predeclared seed 20261014 solely for pair order and arm placement,
not model generation. Writer files use opaque names w17.json and w83.json.
Library writer: one --view drafting bundle per task, exactly one guide,
--limit 2 and --max-chars 24000, task classifications unchanged. Analyses use
experiments.analysis; caption uses experiments.table.efficiency. No full packs,
reference view, author prose, expanded records or iterative scored rewrites.

Decision evidence: all eight raw outputs and hashes, all eight pairwise ratings
with six existing professionalism dimensions and critical-error flags, literal
numeric/condition checks plus manual sentence roles (finding, evidence,
interpretation, boundary, repetition). Fewer numbers is NOT a quality target.
Word count, decimal arithmetic and complete source provenance are objective;
rhetorical ratings and preference are subjective. A missing statistic in a
packet is not evidence that the paper did not compute it. Findings should not
collapse latency, throughput, final performance or online regret.

Report ties and disagreements; adverse flags are not erased by high means.
No p-values, effectiveness certification or human-blind-study claim. Same-family
LLM raters are not independent human reviewers. This public-data transfer is not
validation on the user's manuscript. Private manuscript intake remains open.
Publication PDFs and author paragraphs are temporary, not distributed in repo.

Do not invent results, uncertainty, citations or explanations. The supplied tables and setup remain in the manuscript; an analysis need not repeat every cell. A caption must be interpretable with its table without other prose. Do not claim that a missing statistic was never measured in the source paper. Each response must be 80–130 words. Do not include recommendations, drafting notes, references, or a separate checklist.",

      "target": "One result-analysis paragraph accompanying retained Table T01",
      "domain": "vision_language_action",
      "topic": "action_representation",
      "section": "experiments",
      "intent": "contrast",
      "table_label": "Table T01",
      "setup": "OpenVLA variants on LIBERO. All use parallel decoding and 8-timestep action chunks. Diffusion training uses 50 denoising steps; inference uses DDIM. LIBERO-Long success rates aggregate 500 evaluation episodes (10 tasks × 50); checkpoints were tested every 50K training steps and the best performance selected per run.",
      "columns": ["variant", "test_denoising_steps", "action_throughput_Hz_higher_better", "chunk_latency_seconds_lower_better", "LIBERO_Long_success_percent_higher_better"],
      "rows": [["L1 regression", null, 109.7, 0.0729, 90.7], ["diffusion", 50, 4.2, 1.9070, 91.1], ["diffusion", 10, 19.3, 0.4145, 91.0], ["diffusion", 1, 109.4, 0.0731, 0.0]],

    },
    {
      "task_id": "T02",
      "target": "One self-contained caption for retained Table T02; do not write result-analysis prose",
      "domain": "vision_language_action",
      "topic": "action_representation",
      "section": "experiments",
      "intent": "describe",
      "table_label": "Table T02",
      "setup": "OpenVLA with parallel decoding (PD) versus PD plus action chunking (AC), which generates 8 timesteps per query. Both generate 7-dimensional actions. Inference statistics average 100 queries on an NVIDIA A100; each query uses one 224×224 image and a LIBERO task command. Throughput counts generated actions per second. Latency is seconds per query: one action for PD and an 8-action chunk for PD+AC. LIBERO-Long success rates use 500 evaluation episodes (10 tasks × 50), with the best tested checkpoint selected per run; the number of independent training runs and per-cell uncertainty are not supplied.",
      "columns": ["variant", "action_throughput_Hz_higher_better", "query_latency_seconds_lower_better", "LIBERO_Long_success_percent_higher_better"],
      "rows": [["PD", 15.9, 0.0629, null], ["PD+AC", 108.8, 0.0735, 86.5]],
      "boundary": "The success-rate dash means not reported, not zero or not applicable. Generation throughput is not a measured closed-loop control rate."
    },
    {
      "task_id": "T03",
      "target": "One result-analysis paragraph accompanying retained Table T03",
      "domain": "reinforcement_learning",
      "topic": "rl_theory_evaluation",
      "section": "experiments",
      "intent": "contrast",
      "table_label": "Table T03",
      "setup": "Continual Bench: six sequential manipulation tasks share unified dynamics. This subset compares model-based CEM/MPC planning agents. Average performance (AP) is the mean task success rate over all seen tasks at the final training step. Regret (Reg) is the time-normalized accumulated current-task success shortfall relative to an oracle with success rate 1; it measures online learning, not the complement of final AP. Both are expressed in percent. Perfect Memory trains on all prior data; Coreset uses replay; OA learns an online world model.",
      "columns": ["agent", "final_AP_percent_higher_better", "Reg_percent_lower_better"],
      "rows": [["OA", 72.93, 27.62], ["Perfect Memory", 73.09, 30.95], ["Coreset", 61.83, 30.83]],
      "boundary": "No per-cell uncertainty or significance test is supplied in this packet. These are joint agent/planner results, not isolated world-model prediction errors or measurements of memory and runtime."

      "task_id": "T04",
      "target": "One result-analysis paragraph accompanying retained Table T04",
      "domain": "world_models",
      "topic": "planning_imagination",
      "section": "experiments",
      "intent": "scope",
      "table_label": "Table T04",
      "setup": "CrossTask visual planning with videos: current observation and goal are video clips; a plan contains T actions. Success rate is the percentage of predicted action sequences exactly matching the ground truth. The selected rows use the same ViT-g384 encoder scale. Both methods use frozen encoders pretrained on VideoMix22M and CEM planning. The retained table gives success rates at planning horizons 3, 4, 5 and 6, all higher-is-better.",

    }
  ]
